marker_between: Hebrew "between" framing -- "בין ... ו..." ("between January and March").
"בין" (bein): L. Glinert, *The Grammar of Modern Hebrew*, §9.2 -- בין
"between", coordinating two terms.  (The alternative "בין ... ל..." with the
proclitic ל־ is also standard; here בין pairs with the ו coordinator, which
Glinert notes is equally acceptable: "בין ינואר ומרץ".)
marker_date_lead: Words that open a date or a clock time and belong to it.
Each word is shown opening a time or date phrase on the page named in brackets,
ב: Wiktionary "ב־": "In (a place or time): הם דיברו בבוקר" [he-ב־.wikitext.txt]
marker_from: Hebrew range "from" lead -- opens a bounded or open interval, the correlative
of "to" (עד) in the standard "מ... עד..." range framing ("from January to
March").  Hebrew "from" is the proclitic מ־ (mi-/me-); attached to its noun in
running text ("מינואר") it also appears set off by a maqaf/hyphen
("מ-ינואר"), which the tokenizer treats as a separator, leaving מ as its own
token.  The free form מן is listed for completeness.
מ־ / מן (min): L. Glinert, *The Grammar of Modern Hebrew* (Cambridge UP),
§9.2 -- the inseparable preposition מ־ "from", correlative of עד "until/to"
in ranges of time ("מ... עד..."); מן is its free literary form.
Also: Academy of the Hebrew Language, rulings on the vocalisation of מ־.
marker_half: Hebrew period noun "half" for "the first/second half of <year>" (half_period).
"מחצית"/"חצי": מַחֲצִית = חֵצִי, אחד משני חלקים שווים (Even-Shoshan, מילון
אבן-שושן; the Academy of the Hebrew Language).  The attested surface carries
the definite article ה ("המחצית הראשונה של 2020").
marker_to: Hebrew range "to" boundary -- the term / upper limit of a bounded interval,
correlative of "from" (מ־) in "מ... עד...".  In the "from...to" range framing
the upper bound is realized by עד ("until/up to"), a free word, NOT the
proclitic ל־ (which is directional "to <place>"); "מ... עד..." is the
"עד" (ʿad): L. Glinert, *The Grammar of Modern Hebrew*, §9.2 -- עד "until, up
to", the terminal correlative of מ־ in temporal ranges ("מיום ראשון עד יום
שישי").  Academy of the Hebrew Language, s.v. עד.
marker_to_after_from: Hebrew range "to" boundary that is licensed ONLY after an explicit "from"
lead (מ־/מן) or a "between" lead (בין) -- the proclitic ל־ ("to/for").
ל־ is the everyday directional/dative preposition ("נסעתי לתל אביב" -- "I
travelled to Tel Aviv"; "נתתי לו" -- "I gave to him"), a homograph that is
FAR more common as a plain preposition than as a range terminal.  Registered
globally as a range "to" marker it would fabricate a range out of any bare
"ל־<noun>", so it is kept out of the unconditional ``marker_to`` set (which
holds only עד, the unambiguous "from...until..." terminal) and gated here:
the engine wires these surfaces as range terminators only when a from-lead
(מ־/מן) or a between-lead (בין) sits earlier in the span, exactly the
lead-required guard the Romance directional "a" uses ("de junio a agosto"
fires; a bare "junio a las tres" does not).  So "מ־ינואר ל־אפריל" /
"בין ינואר ל־אפריל" resolve as ranges, while a bare "ל־3 שעות" ("for 3
hours") is left untouched.
The proclitic attaches to its noun in running text ("לאפריל"); set off by a
maqaf/hyphen ("ל-אפריל") the tokenizer leaves ל as its own token, which is
the surface matched here.  The fused form is deliberately NOT split.
"ל־" (le-/la-): L. Glinert, *The Grammar of Modern Hebrew* (Cambridge UP),
§9.2, §12 -- the inseparable preposition ל־ "to, for"; in the alternative
temporal-range framing "מ... ל..." it is the terminal correlative of מ־
"from" (Glinert notes "בין ... ל..." as the equally standard between-form
alongside "בין ... ו...").
Also: Academy of the Hebrew Language, s.v. ל־.

weekday_abbr_0: Hebrew abbreviates a weekday as the day noun plus the letter standing for
its ordinal number -- יום שני is written יום ב׳ ("Days of week on Hebrew
calendar", Wikipedia).  The letter carries a geresh in print; the tokenizer
strips it, so the surface listed here is the bare letter.
